when_to_use: intimate to flowing bossa nova, nylon guitar batida, straight 16ths with a laid-back lead, saudade-leaning AABA arc, 80-160 BPM

defaults.feel: rhythm section dead straight 16ths (no swing), lead/vocal laid-back or rubato, bass anticipation into chord changes

signature_moves: Jobim chromatic descent: Cmaj7 -> C#dim7 -> Dm7 -> D#dim7 -> C/E -> A7(b9,b13)
major-dominant II (Ipanema formula): Fmaj7 -> G7(13) -> Gm9 -> C7(b9)
minor line cliche (saudade): Am9 -> Bm7b5 -> E7(b9,b13) -> Am(maj7) Am6
backdoor + tritone sub: Cmaj9 -> Fm9 Bb13 -> Cmaj7 -> Db13
cadence_options: I - VI - ii - V: Cmaj9 -> A7(b9) -> Dm9 -> G13 G7(b13)
tag ending: vamp the last 2 bars 3x, land on a strummed 6/9 left to ring
avoid: plain triads - always use at minimum a seventh, ninth, or 6/9
swinging the rhythm section - this is a straight-grid genre

hook_archetypes.name: one-note-samba
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a single held or lightly repeated melody note while harmony moves chromatically
hook_archetypes.contour: flat or minimal pitch motion on the lead; motion occurs in the chord line
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Verse A1, over the Jobim chromatic descent

hook_archetypes.name: call-and-batida-response
hook_archetypes.rhythm: 2 bars of lead melody, then 2 bars of lead silence filled by a denser guitar batida
hook_archetypes.contour: the guitar response quotes the melody's rhythm, not its pitch

intro.note_lengths: sparse or absent - batida states the groove alone

verse.note_lengths: sotto voce, mid-length phrases targeting extended tones on chord changes
verse.contour: gentle close-interval movement with minimal leaps
verse.placement: laid-back behind the straight rhythm-section grid

bridge.note_lengths: slightly longer and more harmonically active phrases
bridge.contour: follows denser altered-dominant harmony while remaining restrained
bridge.placement: laid-back, with a small dynamic lift

solo.note_lengths: freer with chromatic passing tones over verse changes
solo.contour: breathy and understated rather than aggressive
solo.placement: rubato phrase edges over an unwaveringly straight rhythm section

drum_skeleton.low_energy: thin cross-stick echoing the batida, shaker constant 16ths, surdo muted on beat 1
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: cross-stick and shaker remain stable, surdo adds a soft accent on beat 3
drum_skeleton.high_energy: optional pandeiro or agogo for 135-160 BPM, still straight 16ths and never swung

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: guitar batida opens solo; shaker enters bar 3; bass enters bar 5; lead enters A1 sotto voce; counter-melody and soft pad enter A2; bridge thickens and contrasts harmonically; A3 is fullest; solo uses verse changes; outro strips to a three-pass tag ending on a ringing 6/9 chord

anti_boredom_rules: only the lead or vocal lays back or goes rubato
use at least one signature harmonic move
dynamics remain restrained for most of the form

bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: supports batida with root on beat 1, chord tone near beat 3, and anticipation into changes
bass_behavior.articulation: short warm acoustic notes with clear separation

groove_intent.feel: straight-sixteenth bossa pulse with a laid-back lead
groove_intent.kick: soft surdo-like pulse rather than a drum-kit backbeat
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: guitar, bass, and percussion remain straight while lead phrases float behind

distinguishing_traits: straight rhythm section with only the lead laying back
chromatic AABA harmony and restrained saudade dynamic
